newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Tudjman to run in '97 elections - interview.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Tudjman to run in '97 elections - interview.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, said to be suffering from incurable stomach cancer, said in a television interview on Friday he planned to run in the country's next presidential elections due in mid-1997.
"If you ask me if I will run in the next presidential elections, the answer is yes," the 74-year old former communist general told CNN television.
Political analysts and diplomats speculated that Tudjman, who steered Croatia to independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991-95, would step down before the presidential elections due in June or July.
He was treated in a U.S. hospital near Washington in November for what U.S. diplomats said was a terminal-stage stomach cancer. Croatian media claimed he had an ulcer.
In an interview with the CNN on Friday Tudjman said the reports about his health were "exaggerated" and that he was performing his duties normally, and even played tennis, his favourite recreation.
In recent weeks Tudjman made systematic attempts to convince the Croatian public that he was not as ill as leaks from the diplomatic and Croatian medical circles had suggested.
